To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of MOAT can help to improve the quality of tags and to create a better connection to Linked Data, and that it is possible to use MOAT in a collaborative way.

(i) MOAT allows users to create interlinked data and let their data enter the Semantic Web; (ii) MOAT allows content producers to give meanings to their free-tags, using URIs; (iii) MOAT is lightweight, as it only uses the most essential Linked Data principles.
MOAT is a lightweight Semantic Web application that allows Web 2. 0 content producers to give meaning to tags in a collaborative way.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the meaning of a tag in a social tagging application? How can we use this meaning to interlink the data produced by these applications to the Linked Data Cloud? How can we let the content producers themselves give meaning to their own tags in an easy and intuitive way?
the following question: How can Web 2. 0 content producers give machine-readable meanings to their tags?
the following question: How to let users create machine-readable data from their tags in a collaborative way?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOAT is an approach for collaborative tagging that allows the user to give a meaning to the tags used.
the MOAT approach is a lightweight framework for the collaborative definition of tag semantics.

this approach is a very good way of making use of the existing Linked Data resources to provide meanings for tags and thus making it possible for the content producers to create interlinked RDF datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework that allows users to give meanings to their content and share it in a machine-readable way.
it provides a way for Web 2. 0 users to contribute Linked Data.

MOAT is a framework that allows content producers to give meanings to tags and to interlink their content in a machine-readable way, while solving the problem of the ambiguity and the heterogeneity of free-tagging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Linked Data principles can be extended to the tagging paradigm to provide a collaborative approach that allows Web 2. 0 content producers to give meanings to their content.
the Linked Data principles can be used as a bridge between Web 2. 0 and Semantic Web, allowing the latter to benefit from the former, while keeping the same level of flexibility and ease of use.
we provide a lightweight way to make the Web more semantic, by letting Web 2. 0 users contribute their knowledge in a collaborative way, and by providing a simple and easy way to let them do it.
